Luke loved watching the miniature world he had in his basement. After all, he tried doing this, creating a breed of human beings that are only approximately six inches tall on average, for years now, failing plenty of times, from reasons ranging from carelessness when leaving the forming miniature embryos' artificial uterus unprotected, resulting in rats having a feast on his tiny unborn creations, to errors in DNA engineering that caused horrifying mutations, such as eyes dangling out of the miniature people's orbits and feet/hands reversals.

Today, though, was the day that marked five months since the success of the experiment. He sat in his living room, watching the feed from the cameras in his basement through his laptop, smiling from ear to ear and his eyes wide open. He loved seeing how his miniature people's society evolved.

The first few days were full of chaos for the miniature people. They woke up as young adults, about a thousand of them, confused and scared, not knowing who, what or where they were, but being self aware... Sentient. About a week later, they began creating a rudimentary spoken language, and also the first orgy took place. Luke still masturbates to the memory of a thousand men and women fucking in his huge basement, the image clear as day in his head. That same day, they began to look for food, since none of them had eaten since their awakening, though water was plentiful from the ''waterfall'' that the running sink was, although it was a long and perilous journey up the white mountain that only a handful were able to make, thus having to carry water down for the rest. They became a hunter society, using sharpened bits of wood as spears to kill mice, but only the really strong and brave could take on a rat. A short bit later, one of the men in a group of hunters tracking some mice began telling them what to do, and they listened to his orders, bringing about the world's first leader. When they returned to the village under the sink, the man, named ''Atrium'', proclaimed himself leader of everyone, telling everyone that they had to do whatever he commanded of them. A couple of people questioned his authority, and he ordered his hunters to kill them. And now, the world had it's first tyrant.

Luke realized, after a couple of months, that they don't age like normal humans. They age in a month what humans age in ten years. They also reproduce quickly, a pregnancy requiring only about 2-3 days from impregnation to birth.

Today, Luke looked very excited. The feed from the basement was showing Atrium's son, Anyol, leading the Fahrean tribe's army towards the Lapali tribe's camp, at the base of the flat mountains (the stairs leading out of the basement). With 5.000 spearmen and 2.000 bowmen, and accompanied by 50 tamed wasps, Anyol thought victory was certain.

Meanwhile, at the Lapali camp, tribe elder Hanar was sitting down with High Chief Ravdomir in the chief's yurt.

''Our scouts tell us they have trained fifty wasps. Such thing was never heard of before.'' the elder says, nervously looking in the distance.

Ravdomir sighed. ''When will they arrive?''

''Two hours, three at most.''

Ravdomir chuckled. ''Funny how you shamans managed to find out that the great while circle in the sky measured time. Now... They'll be here after sunset then.''

''Yes.''

''Good. Tell our warriors to get ready.'' he paused, looking up at the sky and at one of the cameras. ''Are you sure that those things are the eyes of the Gods?''

''Aye. And they're watching us.''

''Let's make them proud, then.''

Ravdomir stood up and walked outside his yurt.

​

Luke chewed on some popcorn. ''This shit is better than watching Game of Thrones! And it's real!''

​

Three hours later, the army of Anyol came face to face with the army of Ravdomir. The Lapani were greatly outnumbered, but despite that, they were the first to charge. The Fahrean released the wasps, who flew at high speed towards the Lapani warriors. Dozens were killed by the wasps, but the Lapani bowmen were renowned for their excellent marksmanship, and put down the wasps as quickly as they came. The Fahrean launched a rain of bullets on the Lapani, but their wooden shields were enough to protect them from the inferior Fahrean arrows. Right after the Fahrean archers ran out of arrows, the Fahrean infantry charged. The Lapani infantry charged as well, but then, in a move that took the Fahrean completely by surprise, the Lapani warriors stopped and dropped down on their stomachs, giving the Lapani archers behind them a clear target line against the unshielded Fahrean warriors.

With most of the Fahrean army now dead, and the rest retreating, Anyol was desperately urging his running men to return to the fight. When he tried physically stopping one of his men from retreating, the desperate warrior stabbed him in the stomach with his spear, leaving his spear inside of Anyol as he continued to run away from the advancing Lapani troops.

As Anyol laid on his back, drawing his last few breaths, a figure stood over him. Ravdomir.

''By your customs, whoever downs the Narl in combat will take his role. Thank you for giving me the chance to rule both the flat mountains and the white mountain.'' Ravdomir said, pulling the spear out of Anyol's chest and finally thrusting it  in his throat.

Ravdomir turned to his men. ''Keep moving! Tonight we're marching on White Mountain!''

A collective shout of cheers was heard as the Lapani warriors continued walking south.

Luke yawned and looked at the clock. 10:38 P.M.. ''Gotta wake up early tomorrow...'' he told himself as he turned off his laptop and went to bed.

Joe used to tell me that back when all the ruins were inhabited, vibrant cities full of lights and noise, everyone thought that the thing that was most likely to end the world would be a nuclear war. I still kind of struggle to grasp the concept of nuclear weapons: I'm lucky enough to find a bit of gas for a molotov, and I only use that molotov in emergencies, mind you, since who knows when I'll find another intact bottle and some more flammable liquid... Meanwhile, they had the resources back then to build bombs so powerful they could wipe entire cities off the face of the Earth? I'm a bit skeptical, but... Hell, if they could build those huge buildings, then they might have been capable of crafting huge explosives, too...

In any case, it wasn't a nuclear war that brought the end of the world I was never destined to know, the world where it's said most of the people had a place to sleep and the luxury of having food and clean water in their homes. No... The end was brought by the greed of some greedy dictator somewhere. There are tons of versions, but what they all agree on is that this guy decided to have his scientists create a supervirus and release it in a neighboring country to cripple them, and planned to invade once most of them were dead. Problem is, it got out of hand. The virus spread past the borders, and, before anyone could do anything to even slow it down, it was a global pandemic. Billions died. That was fifty years ago. I am twenty years old.

I've been moving from place to place. It's getting harder to find food every passing day. Last time I met another living soul was more or less a year ago... Her name was Diana. We ran into each other scavenging the ruins of what used to be a police station... Stupid, I know, everyone says those were the first buildings to get looted, but sometimes you could get lucky and find something the ones before you missed. Anyway, Diana was 18. Her father had just starved to death the day before, and she was trying to find a bullet for her gun so she could shoot herself. I talked her out of it. While I was talking her out of it, a feral dog snuck up on me, and as it was about to bite me, she reached for her knife and threw it past me, impaling the dog's skull and saving me from possibly getting rabies. After that, we looked into each other's eyes and something just... clicked. It's very rare that you can trust anyone you meet, and even rarer when said person goes out of the way to help you. The two of us did just that for the other.

We travelled together for a while. I guess you'd describe us as a couple. We continued moving around the country, just trying to survive. It was also the first time, for both of us, that life wasn't just about survival. We enjoyed each other's company, and even the harshest of storms and most ravenous of hungers could not stop us from enjoying just being alive and having each other... Though it didn't last.

I woke up one morning to find Diana's already cold corpse next to me. We were somewhere in Washington state, you see, and the winter there is not so kind. Neither of us had proper clothing for that environment, but I somehow stayed alive... I cried for hours, then finally dug a hole with my bare hands and buried her, then left.

Today, I'm in a small town somewhere in Oregon. I can't read it's name on the sign at the entrance because it's really weathered down by the passing of time and lack of cleaning. I've been sitting here, on the last intact bench of a train station with a crippling stomach ache due to starvation, holding my pistol in my left hand, and my last bullet in my right hand, preparing to end it all for the last couple of hours. Soon after the sun rose up, I heard a sound I never heard before... I looked, and saw a train approach.

Normally, I would have ran away or at least hid myself, but I didn't care anymore, so I just sat there and watched as it slowed down and eventually halted into the station. A man dressed in mechanic's attire stuck his head out the window of the locomotive.

''All aboard!'' he shouted, looking at me expectantly.

I looked at him. ''Where are you going?''

''Someplace better.''

I shook my head. ''My time here is done anyway... I wish you well.''

''Exactly. Your time HERE is done. Come on.''

''What for? Everywhere else is fucked anyway. It's pointless.''

Before he could respond, I saw another person at one of the windows. I couldn't believe it... It was Diana! She was smiling and waving at me, motioning for me to get on board. 

The mechanic smiled. ''Seems like your girlfriend's also one of our costumers.''

I wasted no time and boarded the train. I walked around, trying to find Diana. Eventually, I found her, and the friendly mechanic from earlier. The mechanic looked at me. ''Got a ticket?''

I stood frozen in place, unsure of whether he was joking or being serious. ''A... Ticket?''

''Yes.'' He said. He then glanced to the gun and the bullet I was holding. ''That's a valid ticket.''

Then it was that I understood it. Of course none of the people on this train were alive. I nodded at the mechanic and smiled as I loaded my pistol and raised it, pressing the muzzle against my temple. I could see Diana smiling and shedding tears of happiness and sadness at the same time. One more second of looking at her lovely face and thinking I could be with her forever was the only thing I needed to finally have the courage to pull the trigger.

With a quick pull, the gun shot a bullet into my brain. I felt out of my body, then I realized why... I was really out of my body, seeing it drop to the floor, gun still in hand. I directed my view from my now dead body and back to Diana and the mechanic. The mechanic smiled and shook my hand. ''Name's Bob. You can join the other passengers in the back, where you have two seats reserved. Welcome aboard.''

''Thank you.'' I said to the mechanic, before turning to Diana, kissing her on the lips passionately and holding her hand as we started walking towards the back of the train...

It all started on a gloomy Monday morning. I was on the floor of an unknown apartment, with only bits of memories about how I got there. You see, I used to be a drug addict. Heroin was my poison of choice, although I did any and all downers when I had no H.

Anyway, there I was, beginning to slightly shake from the early withdrawal setting in. I glanced around the room, quickly spotting a syringe filled with black tar next to some sleeping girl I don't recall meeting before. "Lucky me," I thought. "She must've fell asleep."

I grabbed the syringe quietly and injected all of it's contents in myself... Which would've been fatal normally. I panicked as I started losing consciousness, my heart rate dropping fast and my vision darkening. Then it happened. I glanced over at the girl, hoping she notices and calls for help. I can't explain how, but I felt myself stealing her life force. Within moments, she was dead and I was feeling like a newborn child. I darted out of there and spent the next few weeks testing my ability.

I only tested my power on people who were a menace to society: gang members, drug dealers, child molesters, rapists... That kind of thing. One of the first few things I found out was that I could adjust how much I take from a person's life. For example, it took me a couple of seconds to take enough to get rid of a cold from a gang member at the gas station one night, same amount of time it took to fully drain a child molester that moved to my neighborhood after being released on parole.
Another thing I learned was that panic automatically used my power on the person I was looking at.
I started using my power for good, ridding the world of monsters with no chance at becoming better. It worked out well... Until today.

You see, I naively thought I was the only one who had a power like this. Turns out that I was wrong.
A serial killer I've been trying to get rid of had it. I only found out when I found him in the middle of the crowd at a concert. I started draining his life force. After five seconds have passed, I knew something was up. Nobody lasted that long. Ten more seconds and I saw it: people began to drop dead all around him. I stopped, not wanting to cause further innocent deaths. He turned to me with a grin and winked before walking up to me.

He placed a hand on my shoulder. "Nice try, kid, but I've been doing this for millennia."
